questions.question: Explain using triangle congruence why the image of an object in a plane mirror is always as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
solutionSteps: Model the mirror as a line segment and object/image as points A and B.
Rays from A reflect at O. Normal line at O shows angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
Triangles ACO and BCO share side OC, have 90 degree angles, and equal angles at O.
By ASA, ΔACO ≅ ΔBCO, so AC = BC (CPCT).

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AD is a median. Prove the inequality AB + BC + CA > 2 AD.
solutionSteps: In ΔABD, AB + BD > AD (Sum of two sides > 3rd).
In ΔACD, AC + CD > AD (Sum of two sides > 3rd).
Since BD + CD = BC, we get AB + AC + BC > 2AD.

questions.question: O is a point in a square ABCD such that triangle OAB is equilateral. Show that triangle OCD is isosceles.
solutionSteps: Triangle OAB equilateral => OA = AB, Angle OAB = 60.
In square ABCD, AB = AD, Angle DAB = 90. So OA = AD.
Angle DAO = 90 - 60 = 30. Triangle OAD is isosceles with base angle 75.
Angle ODC = 90 - 75 = 15. Similarly Angle OCD = 15. So OD = OC.

questions.question: ABC and DBC are on the same base BC with A and D on opposite sides. If AB = AC and DB = DC, show that AD is the perpendicular bisector of BC.
solutionSteps: ΔABD ≅ ΔACD by SSS (AB=AC, DB=DC, AD common). So ∠BAD = ∠CAD.
In ΔABM and ΔACM (M is intersection), AB=AC, AM common, ∠BAM = ∠CAM.
ΔABM ≅ ΔACM by SAS. So BM = CM and ∠AMB = 90.

questions.question: ABC is a right triangle with Angle A = 90° and AB = AC. The bisector of A meets BC at D. Prove that BC = 2 AD.
questions.finalAnswer: Proven using property of 45 degree triangles.
solutionSteps: In rt isosceles triangle ABC, angles B = C = 45°. AD bisects A=90, so BAD = CAD = 45°.
In ΔABD, angles are 45, 45, 90. So AD = BD.
In ΔACD, angles are 45, 45, 90. So AD = CD.
BC = BD + CD = AD + AD = 2 AD.
